Finding rationale:
Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience exit from the Agreement or an individual Service Option Attachment on one month's notice at a calendar month end, which is better than the 60–90 day fallback ceiling, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right: its only Agreement-level termination right is for material breach (3.3) and its only unilateral exit is term-end non-renewal on 90 days' notice (3.2). The clause failed the fallback on one material term because the early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A were open-ended, so we cap them at three months' charges for the terminated Services, a basis that reaches all such charges rather than only recurring ones. We also state the convenience qualifier expressly on each termination branch instead of once at the end of the sentence, without altering the one-month notice, the calendar month-end effective date, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out or the §3.3 proviso barring IBM from recovering §3.4(b) charges after its own breach. Preferred remains unmet only on a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges and a flat 30-day anchor; both are noted, not redlined.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0045: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0042: Customer or IBM may terminate this Agreement for material breach of this Agreement by the other upon written notice containing the specific nature and dates of the material breach. The breaching party will have thirty (30) days from receipt of notice to cure such breach, except for nonpayment by Customer, which must be cured within seven (7) business days from receipt of notice. If such breach has not been timely cured, then the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice; provided, however, it is understood that in the event IBM has so breached this Agreement IBM shall not be entitled to recover the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) below.
p0040: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered operative language:
Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
Customer or IBM may terminate this Agreement for material breach of this Agreement by the other upon written notice containing the specific nature and dates of the material breach. The breaching party will have thirty (30) days from receipt of notice to cure such breach, except for nonpayment by Customer, which must be cured within seven (7) business days from receipt of notice. If such breach has not been timely cured, then the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice; provided, however, it is understood that in the event IBM has so breached this Agreement IBM shall not be entitled to recover the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) below.
Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment for convenience (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three months' charges for terminated Services.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] We state expressly that Customer may terminate this Agreement, or any Service Option Attachment, for convenience (the qualifier now appears on each branch rather than only at the end of the sentence), and we cap the open-ended Attachment A early termination charges at three months' charges for the terminated Services, per our fallback position.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered §3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment for convenience ..." — the original already carried the "for convenience" qualifier for both branches; the right covers the Agreement and each Service Option Attachment (the Order Form analogue here).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice is "at least one month's prior written notice" and termination can only take effect "at the end of any calendar month", so the effective exit can be up to roughly 60 days out (e.g., notice on 5 January takes effect 28 February). Not a flat 30-day anchor; the drafter would need to substitute "thirty (30) days' prior written notice" and remove the calendar-month-end effective-date restriction to reach preferred.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: §3.4 contains no refund mechanic at all; it only requires Customer to pay "the applicable early termination charges, if any". No pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only Agreement-level termination right in the cited text is for uncured material breach (§3.3); its only unilateral exit is the §3.2 auto-renewal election given at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term, which is natural-term non-renewal (assessed under RENEWAL), not a mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: §3.4(a) requires "at least one month's prior written notice" with effect at the end of a calendar month — shorter than, and therefore within, the 60–90 day fallback ceiling and more favourable to Customer.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Edited §3.4(b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three months' charges for terminated Services." The cap attaches to all Attachment A / Service Option Attachment early termination charges, not merely recurring ones.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No IBM convenience right exists mid-term: §3.3 permits IBM to terminate only for uncured material breach, and §3.2 permits IBM only to elect non-renewal effective at the end of the then-current term. The mapping's cited quote (§3.3 breach clause) is imprecise evidence, but the substance — absence of any IBM mid-term convenience right — holds on the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: §3.2: IBM must notify "in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term ... that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment." That is the only IBM no-cause exit and it carries a 90-day notice floor.

reasons: Fallback is complete: Customer keeps a one-month convenience exit (better than the 60–90 day ceiling), early termination charges are now capped at three months' charges for the terminated Services, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right — its only no-cause exit is the §3.2 term-end non-renewal on 90 days' notice.

Preferred fails on two elements: there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges on convenience termination, and the notice construct (one month's notice effective only at a calendar month end) can push the exit well past 30 days. To reach preferred the drafter would need to insert a refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period and replace "at least one month's prior written notice ... at the end of any calendar month" with a flat "thirty (30) days' prior written notice".

Minimality fails. Operations 1 and 2 only relocate and duplicate the words "for convenience": the original sentence already read "... or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of ...) for convenience at the end of any calendar month", so the convenience qualifier already governed both branches. The fallback element it was mapped to was already met, making the edit a cosmetic paraphrase that duplicates an operative term outside the only necessary change. Repair by reverting to the original wording of the opening clause and keeping only the §3.4(b) cap.

Intent is preserved: the one-month notice, the calendar month-end effective date, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out and the §3.3 proviso barring IBM from recovering §3.4(b) charges after its own breach all survive without contradiction, and the cap creates no dangling cross-reference to Attachment A.

Deviation status is correct because the pre-edit clause failed the fallback on the uncapped Attachment A early termination charges, but the exposure is narrow (a fee cap only, with the Customer exit and the absence of a Vendor mid-term convenience right already in place), so severity is better characterised as medium.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: 3.1 Term

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-5f0768a6","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.1 Indemnification by IBM","rationale":"Section 8.1 gives us an express IBM defence and indemnity for third-party patent, trademark, copyright and trade-secret claims relating to Materials and Base Components IBM provides or uses in performing the Services, with the usual customer-side exclusions (Customer-provided items incorporated into Materials, Customer modifications, combinations with non-IBM products, and non-IBM hardware/software/data) — the fallback treats these exclusions as permitted, and the absence of an express \"specifications\" exclusion is favourable to us. The fallback remedies are all present: IBM must enable continued use, modify, or replace with functionally equivalent non-infringing items, and if none is reasonably available IBM credits the amounts we paid for the applicable Materials/Base Components (capped at twelve months of charges). On the super-cap element, Section 9.1(a) lists indemnification payments under Section 8.1 as a separate head of liability outside the $100,000/12-months monetary cap in 9.1(c), so IBM's IP indemnity is effectively uncapped — better than the 3× annual fees super-cap the fallback would accept. Notice, IBM control of the defence and our cooperation are the standard procedural conditions (with IBM reimbursing our above-nominal cooperation costs). This therefore sits at the fallback and is acceptable. Short of the preferred position, IBM's indemnity does not extend to breach of applicable law, IBM-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and our Section 8.2 indemnity is wider than Customer content plus breach of law (it also covers Customer Components IP claims, Services Recipient claims and mechanics' liens, mitigated by the 8.2(c) carve-back for IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach); we note these as gaps rather than redlining a bargain that meets the fallback.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-67988114","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.10 Assignment","rationale":"Section 14.10 binds only Customer: we need IBM's consent for any assignment outside the narrow merger/consolidation/acquisition carve-out (so even an intra-group affiliate transfer or a sale of substantially all assets requires consent), while IBM is unrestricted and could assign the Agreement to anyone, including a competitor of ours. That asymmetry fails even the fallback, which requires consent for every non-successor assignment on both sides. The redline leaves our general consent sentence and the not-unreasonably-withheld standard untouched, widens the existing \"Notwithstanding\" carve-out to affiliates and asset sales, and adds the IBM-side consent requirement, absolute competitor bar, and confirmation that a change of control of Bluefly gives IBM no termination right (no such right exists today, so that sentence is confirmatory).","proposal":"Keep our general consent sentence; extend the existing carve-out to affiliates and asset sales, and add IBM-side consent, no-competitor and no-change-of-control-termination language.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-c7bc3924","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.16 Freedom of Action","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-source or requirements obligation on Bluefly. Searches for \"exclusive\", sole-supplier, requirements-volume and third-party-procurement language returned only (i) tax charges being \"exclusive of\" taxes, (ii) the § 5.2 exclusive-warranty disclaimer, and (iii) nonexclusive licences granted to Customer (§ 12.1, § 5.4) — none of which restrict Customer's sourcing. Affirmatively, § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) confirms each party may enter into similar agreements with others, so Bluefly may buy hosting from other suppliers. The only Customer-side restrictions are § 14.11 (no resale of the Services) and the § 12.1 licence-scope limits, which are use/resale restrictions, not exclusive dealing. This meets the preferred position; no redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-592913c0","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Other Disclaimers","rationale":"Section 7.0 (Materials) is the only ownership/licence architecture in this hosting agreement. IBM correctly retains ownership of its pre-existing and generic Type II Materials, and Customer takes ownership of Type I Materials, so the walk-away (assignment of Customer IP) is not triggered. But the deliverable licence fails the fallback on material terms: the Type II licence is not perpetual, is confined to Customer's Enterprise only, and omits any right to modify or sublicense, so we could not adapt or share delivered reports, programs and documentation for our business. Separately, § 14.18 gives IBM and its Enterprise a standing right to store and use Customer contact information \"anywhere they do business\", to pass it to contractors, Business Partners and assignees for their \"collective business activities\" including promotions and marketing research - independent exploitation of Customer data well beyond processing to provide the Services. The redline makes the Type II licence perpetual, royalty-free and modifiable/sublicensable for our business, and confines IBM's rights in our Content, Customer Components and other Customer data to processing solely to provide the Services. We have not disturbed IBM's ownership of Type II Materials, the revocable Base Components platform licence in § 12.1 (its own hosting platform), or the Type I licence-back in § 7(b), none of which the selected checklist reaches.","proposal":"Broaden the Type II Materials licence to a perpetual, royalty-free right to use, modify, distribute and sublicense for Customer's business, and limit IBM's rights in Customer data to providing the Services.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-085bf5ae","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.1 License","rationale":"Section 12.1 grants only Customer (Bluefly) a \"revocable\" licence to the Base Components; it names neither Affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf, and Section 14.17 confirms no other licences are implied, so there is no path to add them. A licence revocable at IBM's discretion with affiliates and contractors excluded is walk-away territory and also fails the fallback (no affiliate coverage even on written notice). Successor transferability is already satisfied by Section 14.10, which lets Customer assign the Agreement to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so we have not touched it. The redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, deletes \"revocable\", and adds perpetuity/irrevocability for paid-up licences with breach-only termination for subscription licences.","proposal":"Extend the Base Components licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove at-will revocability","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-ab397129","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.16 Freedom of Action","rationale":"No non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for compete/competing/competitor, \"shall not\" prohibitions, exclusivity, sole-source and field-of-use/territory language returned no restraint on Bluefly's business. To the contrary, § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) expressly confirms that \"Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others,\" so Customer remains free to buy or build competing hosting solutions. The only Customer-side prohibitions are licence-scope terms rather than restrictive covenants: § 14.11 bars reselling the Services, § 12.1 limits use of IBM's Base Components to use \"solely in connection with the Services\", and § 14.19 merely limits where IBM delivers. None of these restricts the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, so the clause meets the preferred position and no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-54ffa9fd","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11.3 Suspected Violations","rationale":"Section 11.3 is the only right binding Customer that operates as an inspection/verification right: IBM may investigate suspected AUP violations without any frequency limit, without prior notice (notice is only \"attempt[ed]\" before restricting access or removing Content, and not for the investigation itself), and with no cost allocation, reinforced by Customer's open-ended obligation in p0138 to supply \"all relevant information ... at IBM's request.\" Unlimited and unannounced verification is walk-away territory under AUDIT, so we redline to the fallback: once per year, 15 days' prior notice, and IBM bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%. We have not proposed the preferred independent-auditor, off-site or no-system-access terms, which remain available if IBM will not accept the fallback wording.","proposal":"Add frequency, notice and cost limits to IBM's investigation/verification right in 11.3","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-b39f640d","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.3 Choice of Law","rationale":"§ 14.3 selects New York substantive law, which matches our preferred governing law. However, the Agreement nowhere designates a dispute forum: searches for venue, jurisdiction, courts, dispute, and arbitration return only the severability and indemnity references to a \"court of competent jurisdiction\" (p0175, p0089, p0098), and §§ 14.4 (jury waiver) and 14.14 (two-year actions period) do not fix a forum. With no exclusive court venue, the clause fails both the preferred and the fallback forum element on a material term, leaving venue open to Vendor-favourable forum selection. We therefore add the shortest venue sentence at the preferred level (exclusive state and federal courts in New York County, with the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out) and leave the New York law sentence verbatim. The jury waiver and limitation period are noted only, not redlined.","proposal":"Add exclusive New York County court venue to the Choice of Law clause","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-6ce44e81","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 14.12 Risk of Loss","rationale":"No insurance clause exists anywhere in the Agreement: searches for insurance, coverage and certificates return nothing, and the closest candidates (14.12 Risk of Loss, 5.3 Security, 14.18 Data Protection) allocate risk and describe security/processing without any coverage undertaking. IBM hosts the e-business Hosting Environment and processes personal information on our behalf (14.18), which is walk-away territory under the rule, so we insert the preferred coverage package as new Section 14.21 (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where IBM processes our data, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). The cyber trigger is drafted to reach all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for us since \"Customer Data\" is not a defined term here.","proposal":"Insert a new Section 14.21 requiring IBM to carry CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy and workers' compensation insurance and to provide certificates on request.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-dbcc98c3","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability","rationale":"Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose mirror-image caps on IBM and on Customer at the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid in the preceding 12 months, so the cap is mutual and 12-month-fees based, indemnification payments sit outside that cap as a separate liability item (9.1(a)/9.2(a)), and Section 10 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually. However, the caps contain no carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and Section 6 expressly makes Sections 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment, so confidentiality breaches are capped. That fails the fallback checklist on a material term. We propose one short mutual carve-out sentence at the fallback level rather than upgrading the cap formula; the $100,000 floor (versus our preferred USD 1,000,000) and the absence of data-protection and IP-infringement carve-outs are noted but not pressed here.","proposal":"Add mutual carve-out from the Section 9 caps for confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-dda3cc25","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.16 Freedom of Action","rationale":"We searched the Charges and Payment provisions (§§ 4.1–4.2), the pricing-amendment mechanics (§ 13.1, § 13.3) and the whole agreement for any best-price, most-favoured-customer, disclosure or right-to-match undertaking. There is none: charges run one way (IBM invoices Customer at the rates in the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms), IBM's only pricing right is a forward-looking price change after 12 months with 90 days' notice and a Customer termination right, and § 14.16 confirms each party remains free to contract with others. Customer therefore carries no MFN obligation benefiting IBM, which satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-86ddcdeb","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4.1 Charges","rationale":"The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic. Charges under § 4.1 arise only for Services actually ordered (via Order Forms and Service Option Attachments) and are specified as one-time, installment, recurring or usage, so Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services — the preferred position. Targeted searches for \"minimum\", \"commit to purchase\", \"take or pay\", \"shortfall\" and usage/volume caps returned nothing, and § 11.5 (Capacity Planning) only allocates responsibility for sizing capacity, imposing no committed capacity on Customer. Customer additionally holds an exit under § 3.4 (termination for convenience on one month's notice at the end of any calendar month), and § 3.2 renewal is terminable by either party on 90 days' notice. Minor point noted only: § 3.4(b) refers to early termination charges \"if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments\" — Attachment A is not included in the reviewed text, so we should confirm on diligence that no early termination charge operates as a de facto commitment. That contingent reference is not itself a minimum commitment and does not warrant a redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-60b73072","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.8 Personnel","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"employ or engage\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"personnel\", \"employees\" and related terms return no hiring or solicitation restriction anywhere in the Agreement. § 14.8 (Personnel) addresses only supervision, assignment and subcontracting; § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) confirms each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the IBM hosting agreement — 18 rules assessed

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Base Terms against 18 playbook rules. Eight clauses are acceptable as drafted (indemnification, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments, non-solicitation, and the absence of Customer-side restraints generally); seven are deviations we propose to redline; two are missing clauses that must be inserted; and two require further review before we send comments.

The commercially significant points are:

- **Licence scope (§ 12.1)** — the Base Components licence is *revocable* at IBM's discretion and names neither our Affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf. This is walk-away territory and our top priority.
- **No insurance obligation anywhere in the Agreement** — IBM hosts our environment and processes personal information on our behalf (§ 14.18) with no coverage undertaking. Also walk-away territory; we insert the preferred coverage package.
- **No transition assistance or data return/deletion mechanic** — § 3.5 covers only accrued payments. Unacceptable for a hosted service; we insert a new § 3.6.
- **Audit/investigation right (§ 11.3)** — IBM may investigate suspected AUP violations without frequency limit, without prior notice and with no cost allocation. Walk-away territory; we redline to the fallback (annual, 15 days' notice, IBM bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%).
- **Assignment asymmetry (§ 14.10)** — we need consent for almost any transfer; IBM is unrestricted and could assign to a competitor.
- **Liability caps (§§ 9.1–9.2)** are mutual and 12-month-fees based with indemnities outside the cap (favourable), but confidentiality breaches are capped and there is no gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-out.
- **Governing law (§ 14.3)** selects New York law (our preference) but the Agreement designates no forum at all; we add exclusive New York County venue.

On the favourable side, IBM's IP indemnity (§ 8.1) is effectively uncapped, we hold a one-month convenience exit (§ 3.4), and no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicit obligation binds us.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary of position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback) | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | Express IP defence and indemnity with permitted customer-side exclusions; all fallback remedies present; § 9.1(a) places indemnity payments outside the monetary cap, so effectively uncapped. Noted only: no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross-negligence indemnity, and our § 8.2 indemnity is broader than preferred. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | Consent obligation binds Customer only (with a narrow merger carve-out); IBM may assign freely, including to a competitor. Fails the fallback, which requires mutual consent for non-successor assignments. Redline: extend the carve-out to affiliates and asset sales, add IBM-side consent, a competitor bar, and confirmation that a change of control gives IBM no termination right. *(Verification: repaired.)* |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (§ 7.0 Materials; § 14.18) | Ownership split is acceptable (we own Type I; IBM owns Type II), so the walk-away is not triggered. But the Type II licence is not perpetual, is confined to our Enterprise, and omits modification and sublicensing rights; § 14.18 lets IBM and its Enterprise use our contact information for marketing and research. Redline: perpetual, royalty-free, modifiable/sublicensable Type II licence and IBM data rights limited to providing the Services. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 12.1 License | Base Components licence is *revocable*, runs to Bluefly only, and § 14.17 bars implied licences, so Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no cure. Redline: extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, delete "revocable", add perpetuity for paid-up licences and breach-only termination for subscriptions. Successor transfer is already covered by § 14.10. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements obligation; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. § 14.11 (no resale) and § 12.1 scope limits are use restrictions, not exclusive dealing. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint. § 14.11, § 12.1 and § 14.19 are licence-scope and delivery-location terms only. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | Unlimited, unannounced investigation right with no cost allocation, reinforced by our open-ended obligation to supply all relevant information on request. Redline to the fallback: once per year, 15 days' prior notice, IBM bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%. Preferred independent-auditor/off-site terms held in reserve. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York substantive law matches our preference, but no forum is designated anywhere (only generic "court of competent jurisdiction" references). Redline: add exclusive state and federal courts in New York County with the customary injunctive-relief carve-out; law sentence untouched. Jury waiver (§ 14.4) and two-year limitation (§ 14.14) noted only. |
| Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away)** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance clause exists; § 14.12, § 5.3 and § 14.18 allocate risk and describe security without any coverage undertaking. Insert new § 14.21: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Caps are mutual at the greater of USD 100,000 or 12 months' charges, indemnities sit outside the cap and consequential damages are mutually excluded — but confidentiality breaches are capped (§ 6 makes §§ 9–10 prevail over the NDA) and there is no gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-out. Redline: one mutual carve-out sentence at the fallback. USD 100,000 floor and absence of data-protection/IP carve-outs noted, not pressed. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Only a reasonable care and skill undertaking, with no warranty period, no conformance-to-documentation warranty and no remedy; §§ 5.2 and 5.4 make it exclusive and add "AS IS" disclaimers. Redline inside § 5.1 (to sit within the § 5.2 carve-in): 90-day software conformance warranty, 30-day Services warranty, repair/replace-or-refund remedy. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 covers accrued payments only; no exit assistance, export, return or deletion obligation anywhere. Insert new § 3.6: six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of Content in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter (using the defined term "Content"). |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Needs review** | § 3.2 Renewal | Automatic renewal with a 90-day non-renewal notice window exceeds our 60-day fallback ceiling. Single numeral edit proposed to reach the fallback. No renewal price-increase mechanic exists, so the uplift element is satisfied. Escalation point: any Service Option Attachment with a term over 12 months produces an automatic multi-year renewal. *(Verification: fail — must be re-run before issue.)* |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Our one-month convenience exit is better than the fallback and IBM has no mid-term convenience right. The failure is the open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A; proposed cap of three months' charges for the terminated Services. Pro-rata refund of prepaid charges noted, not redlined. *(Verification: fail — must be re-run before issue.)* |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No best-price, most-favoured-customer, disclosure or right-to-match undertaking. IBM's only pricing right is a forward-looking change after 12 months on 90 days' notice with a Customer termination right. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant (preferred) | § 4.1 Charges | Charges arise only for Services actually ordered; no minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic; § 11.5 allocates capacity planning only. We hold exits under §§ 3.2 and 3.4. Diligence point: Attachment A (not in the reviewed text) may contain early termination charges. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.8 Personnel | No solicitation, no-hire or recruitment restriction; § 14.8 addresses supervision and subcontracting only. Resist introduction; if added, hold to the mutual 12-month fallback with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) conditions our convenience exit on uncapped early termination charges set in documents outside the Base Terms, and nothing makes this the sole liquidated amount. Redline to the fallback (three months' charges, sole liquidated amount) rather than deletion, because § 3.3 cross-refers to § 3.4(b). Late payment fees (§ 4.2) and the § 9.2 cap are not liquidated damages. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They should be resolved before signature and, if IBM refuses, escalated rather than conceded.

1. **§ 12.1 — revocable licence excluding Affiliates and contractors.** A licence revocable at IBM's discretion, with no affiliate or contractor coverage and no implied licences (§ 14.17), is walk-away territory and also fails the fallback.
2. **No insurance obligation (absence; nearest provision § 14.12).** IBM hosts our environment and processes personal information on our behalf with no coverage undertaking — walk-away territory under the rule.
3. **§ 11.3 — unlimited, unannounced investigation right.** Verification without frequency limits, prior notice or cost allocation is walk-away territory; the fallback (annual / 15 days / cost shifting) is our landing zone.
4. **§ 3.2 — multi-year automatic renewal exposure (escalation).** Any Service Option Attachment with a term exceeding 12 months would auto-renew for that multi-year period. Fix with a 12-month renewal cap or escalate.

For completeness: the IP walk-away (assignment of Customer IP) is **not** triggered — we take ownership of Type I Materials under § 7.0.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-run verification on the two `needs_review` items (RENEWAL § 3.2 and T4C § 3.4)** before any markup leaves our side; both currently carry a failed verification and should not be issued as drafted.
2. **Obtain Attachment A and all Service Option Attachments / Order Forms.** They drive the early termination charges under §§ 3.3, 3.4(b) (relevant to both T4C and LD), the pricing under § 4.1, and the attachment terms that determine the § 3.2 renewal exposure. We cannot close MINCOMMIT, T4C or LD without them.
3. **Issue the redline in priority order:** § 12.1 licence scope, new insurance section (§ 14.21), new transition/data-return section, § 11.3 audit limits, § 14.10 assignment mutuality, § 9 confidentiality and wilful misconduct carve-out, § 5.1 warranties, § 14.3 venue, Type II licence and § 14.18 data-use limits, § 3.4(b) charge cap.
4. **Confirm the confidentiality interaction.** Section 6 makes §§ 9 and 10 prevail over the separate confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment; confirm with the deal team whether any separate NDA terms need conforming.
5. **Hold reserve positions.** For AUDIT we have not yet asked for independent-auditor, off-site or no-system-access terms; for WARRANTY we have targeted the fallback only. Both remain available if IBM resists.
6. **Watch-list for negotiation:** resist any late introduction of exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicitation language — we currently sit at the preferred position on all five."}
